title: Ang 728–729: Suhi begins
hook: Guru Nanak opens the raga of union
tomorrow: if someone guards your head, can anything still go wrong?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Tilang closed with a Guru, a weaver and a printer: even now, nothing is lost. Three voices. Today a new raga opens, and it opens with a puzzle.

Cheap jewelry looks great under store lights. A week later, there's a dark ring on your finger. Suhi, the raga of union, begins on ang 728, and a page later Guru Nanak points at something shiny. In paraphrase: bronze is bright and gleaming, but rub it, and its blackness comes off on your hand; wash it again and again, and it's still not clean. So here's the puzzle: why would a raga of union start by rubbing black off bronze?
screen: `A DARK RING ON YOUR FINGER.` → `BRIGHT BRONZE, BLACK ON THE HAND.` → `WHY START A RAGA OF UNION HERE?`

segments.voice: Tradition tells the story behind it. Guru Nanak and his companion Mardana stopped at a rest-house kept by a man called Sajjan, a name that means friend. It looked like a welcoming place on the road, tradition says, with a place to pray for Hindus and a place for Muslims. At night, Sajjan robbed his guests, and worse. When the Guru's turn came, he sang. Bright bronze that leaves black on your hand. And then, in paraphrase, the line that turned the story: those are my friends, my sajjan, who go along with me, and who stand with me where the account is called. Tradition says Sajjan heard his own name in the hymn, fell at the Guru's feet, and changed his life. So, the puzzle. Union in Suhi doesn't start with shine. A surface can look welcoming and still leave a mark. The bride songs of this raga come later; Guru Nanak begins with what makes a friend a friend. Not the gleam, but the one who walks with you all the way, to where the account is asked. Union.
screen: `A REST-HOUSE KEPT BY SAJJAN.` · `WELCOMING OUTSIDE, BLACK INSIDE.` · `FRIENDS WALK WITH YOU ALL THE WAY.` · `SAJJAN HEARS HIS OWN NAME.` · then, large: `UNION.`

segments.voice: Stand and walk slowly, in the room or a hallway, letting the breath set the pace. Every few steps, bring to mind one person who has walked with you when it counted. If walking isn't easy right now, rest your hands on your knees and walk the route in your mind.
Ang 728. Where Suhi begins, the raga of union, and a page on, Guru Nanak's friend who walks with you all the way.
Union: the shine doesn't make the friend; the walking does. Day fifteen thirty-five, side by side.

screen: `DAY 1535 COUNTS.` → `A WALK THROUGH THE GRANTH · 89 OF 180.` → `TOMORROW: IF YOUR HEAD IS GUARDED, CAN ANYTHING GO WRONG?`

howItsDone: Sikhs tell the Janamsakhi story of Guru Nanak and Sajjan, and the Suhi hymn on ang 729, with its line about friends who walk with you, is sung in kirtan.

fork.setup: your new friend group is fun and always posting together. your old friend is quieter, but shows up every time things go wrong. her recital is the same night as their party. what fits ang 729?
options: go to the recital; a friend is the one who walks with you.
go to the party; new friendships need more effort early on.
skip both so nobody feels you chose one over the other.
fork.reveal: Guru Nanak's test isn't the shine: friends are the ones who go along with you and stand with you where the account is asked.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 written: shape puzzle (why does a raga of union open on bronze that leaves black?). New part: Suhi to Gond (ang 728–875). Simran arc: the milni, Navi's in-laws seem polished.
Sajjan story told as tradition: 'robbed his guests, and worse' keeps the killings unstated for younger listeners. Confirm tone and the detail of a place to pray for Hindus and for Muslims.
'Wash it again and again' paraphrases 'je sau dhovaa' (even if washed a hundred times); the number is left out. Confirm the ang 729 paraphrase.
The opening hymn on ang 728 ('bhaandaa dhoe bais dhoop devahu', washing the vessel and setting the milk) is not taught today; only noted that Suhi begins there.
2026-10-15 (job 3, new lesson recipe): chat, gloss and recall written with the lesson; confirm the chat reply, glosses, scripts and pronunciations with the Keeper.
